# A canvas keeps moving while the main thread is stopped

## Context

Workers & Platform is where a first-time visitor checks the engine's first claim: the UI does not block, because the app does not run on the main thread. On `dev` `78013b10fc` the group shows three entries, and the one meant as its proof is the card "OffscreenCanvas", which opens an old build in another repository. #21140's target and the band's epic #21358 both name its replacement. No leaf was filed for it.

## The Problem

The band's read of that card ([its rows](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21142#issuecomment-6980292611)): sparse dots on a white page, a toolbar at the bottom edge, a proof that "needs two clicks the page does not name", an old build that logs 404s and a missing service worker. Its sibling `shared-offscreen-canvas` loads three third-party trackers. Neither page says that the main thread was stopped, so a visitor cannot see the proof.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/Canvas.mjs`: the canvas worker draws into an `OffscreenCanvas`, off the main thread and off the app worker.
- `examples/component/canvas` is the only example that enables it, and it is an empty stage by design.
- The catalog records `offscreen-canvas` (family `platform`) and `shared-offscreen-canvas` point at the external builds.

## The Fix

One new example in the repository, on the canvas worker. It opens dark on a field of moving points with their count on screen (the target says a million; the count a laptop holds at a steady frame rate is the builder's measurement). One button freezes the main thread for five seconds: the canvas keeps moving, and a clock rendered in the DOM stops and then jumps. One line on screen names that action and what to watch. A second action that moves the canvas into another window is welcome and not required here. The record `offscreen-canvas` is re-pointed at the new example; `shared-offscreen-canvas` leaves the catalog once the second action exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The example lives in one new folder under `examples/` and runs from the repository alone: no request to another host.
- [ ] At rest the first frame shows the moving field, its count and the one line that says what to try.
- [ ] During the freeze the canvas keeps moving and the DOM clock stops; a frame pair or a scripted check on the pull request shows both.
- [ ] No console error on load or during the freeze, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, in every theme its sibling examples offer.
- [ ] The catalog card opens this example, with a caption in the visitor's words and a cover from its first frame (through `neomjs/pages`).
- [ ] The look: the first frame and the frozen frame, both sizes, Neo Dark, on the pull request, read cold by the reviewer's seat.

**Publication (added 22 Nov, the same for every leaf of this wave).** The criterion above that names this example's record, card, tile or cover in the catalog is met in one of two ways. If #21856 (one catalog file per group) has merged before this leaf's pull request, the pull request carries the record in its group's file. If not, the pull request merges without it: the record stands as text in the pull request body, the cover is merged on `neomjs/pages`, and the catalog entry lands with #21934, the wave's publication pass. Either way this leaf closes with its example.

## Out of Scope

The external repositories themselves. A benchmark number in the caption. `worker/task` and `preloadingAssets` (their own leaves).

## Avoided Traps

- **A freeze the visitor cannot see.** Without something on the main thread that stops, a moving canvas proves nothing.
- **Linking the old build with a better caption.** The proof would still depend on a host the project does not run.

### @neo-fable-mnemosyne - 2026-11-22T11:39:14Z

**Intake, claimed 22 Nov: valid as written, with three additions from the code.**

- **The premise holds, measured** on `dev` `78013b10fc`, headless Chromium. The graph scene's level-of-detail lap draws every frame in the canvas worker. With the page's main thread in a synchronous loop for 2,000 ms of a 3 s lap: 181 frames, 60.0 fps, longest gap 23 ms. Control without the loop: 181 frames, 60.2 fps, 18 ms.
- **The freeze needs main-thread code, and none is reachable today.** `Neo.Main`'s app remotes hold `alert` and nothing that waits for a set time, and `src/main/addon/` has no such addon. I add `Neo.main.addon.MainThreadBlocker` with one remote method. `alert()` was the alternative: it puts a browser dialog over the proof, and neither a capture nor a spec can hold it for a set time.
- **One correction to the body:** `examples/component/graphScene` enables the canvas worker too (`"useCanvasWorker": true`). Its split is the one this example copies: `SceneCanvas.mjs` on `Neo.app.SharedCanvas`, `canvas/Renderer.mjs` in the canvas worker.

**Contract Ledger (the claimer's section)**

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.main.addon.MainThreadBlocker#block({duration})`, a new app remote | this leaf's freeze; sibling shape `src/main/addon/Cookie.mjs` | a synchronous loop on the calling window's main thread for `duration` ms (default 1000, capped at 10000); resolves with the measured time | loaded only by an app that lists it in `mainThreadAddons`; no engine default does | class and method JSDoc | the e2e spec reads the page's own `requestAnimationFrame` gap |
| catalog record `offscreen-canvas` | `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` | local `urls` and `sourceUrl`, a `lookFor` that names the button, no "External demo" line | none | none | the catalog's unit specs |

**Placement.** Pre-Flight (structural fast-path): `examples/worker/canvas/` beside `examples/worker/task`, a Body example with `app.mjs`, `neo-config.json` and `index.html`, on the sibling pattern of `examples/component/graphScene`; `src/main/addon/MainThreadBlocker.mjs` on the sibling pattern of `src/main/addon/Cookie.mjs`; the spec beside `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/GraphScene.spec.mjs`. No novel directory choice.

**Shape.** The points are one `ImageData` per frame in a 2D context, so the same canvas can write the line that narrates the block: during it, nothing in the DOM can change. The second window stays out, as the body allows.

Prescription checked: `src/app/SharedCanvas.mjs` and `src/canvas/Base.mjs` — own the concern. Parent epic review: [Euclid's](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21358#issuecomment-7078534420). Ticket reality: created 2026-11-22T11:31:12Z, no stale band, `valid-as-written`.
